title: Prepare: Gold Prices are Set to Skyrocket on THIS DATE.
speaker: Kevin Paffrath

macro_themes.view: Gold peaks about 3-5 years after the Fed's money printer expands, so a no-QE Warsh regime is bearish for gold.
Kevin Warsh as Fed chair (to May 2030) will usher in low money printing and deflation, positive for AI and corporations.
An Iran deal would lift bond prices and lower yields rather than lift gold.
Post-build-out AI and job losses are likely deflationary.

calls.condition: Bearish until Warsh turns on QE in a severe recession or is replaced; next gold peak possibly 2033-2035 if printing restarts ~2030.
calls.reason: No money printing under Warsh, clear downtrend in momentum, and lag between QE and gold peaks; bearish since Jan 30.
calls.quote: when you combine Warsh with timing of money printer and momentum you have a bearish outlook

calls.condition: Ahead of an anticipated Iran deal.
calls.reason: Prefers buying the semiconductor dip before an Iran deal; Warsh-driven deflation is positive for the AI trade.
calls.quote: I'd rather buy the dip on semiconductors before an anticipated Iran deal. And I'd rather buy semiconductors than gold.

calls.condition: If an Iran deal happens, bond prices rise and yields fall.
calls.reason: Lack of money printing seen as fiscal responsibility, so bonds benefit after an Iran deal.
calls.quote: what goes up after an Iran deal are bonds. So, the prices of bonds go up. The yields of bonds come down.

notes: Gold $4,122 (-1.3%) was quoted on the hot-CPI day, likely Wed 2026-10-14, so recording may predate listing date. Semis call is sector-level; SMH used as proxy ticker. 4,300/4,500 are Kalshi strike levels, not his targets.
